title: Removing embedded points lowers the support dimension of the kernel
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] and $\mathcal F$ a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Among coherent subsheaves $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal F$ whose support is nowhere dense in $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ there is a maximal one. For $\mathcal F'=\mathcal F/\mathcal K$, one has $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F')=\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$, $\mathcal F'$ has no embedded associated points, and there is a dense open $U\subseteq X$ such that $U\cap\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ is dense in $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ and $\mathcal F'|_U\cong\mathcal F|_U$, and $\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal K))<\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F))$ when the latter dimension is finite and positive.

proof.text: Coherence is equivalent to quasi-coherence plus finite type on X. Every affine coordinate ring is Noetherian and the section module is finite. Apply the affine embedded-prime removal theorem separately on every affine open to choose maximal nowhere-dense submodules N(V), whose quotients have the original support and minimal associated primes.

source.place: Tag 02OL, proof of lemma-remove-embedded-points; uses Algebra Tag 02M7

proof.text: Apply the canonical affine-maxima gluing lemma to obtain a coherent subobject K with affine section ranges N(V). The finite-type support criterion identifies the stalk support on V with the module support under V = Spec Gamma(X,V). These homeomorphisms transfer nowhere density in both directions. Thus K has nowhere-dense support globally. A coherent subobject L containing K and with nowhere-dense support has affine section ranges containing N(V) and nowhere dense in the section support. Local maximality gives range equality. To conclude L <= K, compose its inclusion with the cokernel projection of K; this vanishes on affine sections and hence on all sections by sheaf separation. The kernel-of-cokernel property for a monomorphism factors L through K. This proves global maximality in Lean.

proof.text: The quotient Q = coker(K -> F) is coherent. The affine cokernel formula identifies Gamma(Q,V) linearly with Gamma(F,V)/N(V). Transport the affine support equality and associated-prime minimality through these equivalences. The affine support criterion gives equality of the global stalk supports.

source.place: Tag 02OL, proof of lemma-remove-embedded-points; uses Algebra Tag 02M7

proof.text: Take U to be the complement of the closed stalk support T of K. Injectivity on stalks puts T in Supp(F); its nowhere density there implies nowhere density in X. Hence U is dense in X and in Supp(F). K restricts to zero on U: every restricted section has zero germ everywhere, so is zero by the sheaf axiom. Restriction preserves cokernels, and the cokernel of the resulting zero map is F restricted to U. The restricted cokernel projection is an isomorphism, giving the asserted comparison.

source.place: Tag 02OL, proof of lemma-remove-embedded-points; uses Algebra Tag 02M7

proof.text: Realize the closed support S = Supp(F) as the underlying space of the reduced closed subscheme defined by its vanishing ideal. Its inclusion is a closed immersion, so this subscheme is locally Noetherian, and the inclusion gives a homeomorphism onto S (Mathlib IdealSheafData.subscheme, range_subschemeiota and coe_support_vanishingIdeal). Finite dimension d forces the subscheme nonempty, since empty has dimension bottom. Pull back the closed nowhere-dense subset T = Supp(K), apply the existing scheme dimension-drop theorem, and transfer its conclusion along the embeddings and homeomorphisms. Empty T and d = 0 are handled by the same argument; the public statement still assumes d > 0.

lean.statement: theorem exists_maximal_nowhereDense_support_cokernel (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules) (hF : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace F) : ∃ K : Subobject F, Maximal (fun L : Subobject F ↦ RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace (L : X.Modules) ∧ IsNowhereDense {x : {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (F.presheaf.stalk x)} | ¬ Subsingleton ((L : X.Modules).presheaf.stalk x.val)}) K ∧ {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton ((cokernel K.arrow : X.Modules).presheaf.stalk x)} = {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (F.presheaf.stalk x)} ∧ (∀ (V : X.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen V) (p : Ideal Γ(X, V)), p ∈ associatedPrimes Γ(X, V) Γ((cokernel K.arrow : X.Modules), V) → Minimal (fun q : Ideal Γ(X, V) ↦ q ∈ associatedPrimes Γ(X, V) Γ((cokernel K.arrow : X.Modules), V)) p) ∧ (∃ U : X.Opens, Dense (U : Set X) ∧ Dense {x : {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (F.presheaf.stalk x)} | x.val ∈ U} ∧ Nonempty ((cokernel K.arrow : X.Modules).over U ≅ F.over U)) ∧ (∀ d : ℕ, 0 < d → topologicalKrullDim {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (F.presheaf.stalk x)} = (d : WithBot ℕ∞) → topologicalKrullDim {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton ((K : X.Modules).presheaf.stalk x)} < topologicalKrullDim {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (F.presheaf.stalk x)})
